request.system: You are an expert in clinical classification systems.

messages.content:
ICD-10-AM is the Australian modification of the International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems, 10th revision. Its disease codes are arranged in chapters, and a three-character category is written as one capital letter followed by two digits. The letter indicates the chapter or block: A and B are infectious diseases, C is malignant neoplasms, D is other neoplasms and blood disorders, E is endocrine, nutritional and metabolic disease, F is mental and behavioural disorders, G is the nervous system, H is the eye and ear, I is the circulatory system, J is the respiratory system, K is the digestive system, L is the skin, M is the musculoskeletal system, N is the genitourinary system, O is pregnancy and childbirth, P is the perinatal period, Q is congenital malformations, R is symptoms and abnormal findings, S and T are injury and poisoning, and Z is factors influencing health status. The two digits narrow the chapter to a specific category, for example J44 is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and N17 is acute kidney failure.

The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Using that structure, assign the three-character ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. Choose the chapter letter first, then the two digits.

Hospital course:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY:

Patient:
• Name: Not provided
• Age: 24-year-old
• Gender: Male

Hospitalization Dates:
• Admission: [not provided]
• Discharge: POD #20
Admission Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Hospital Course:
• Patient underwent uncomplicated orthotopic liver transplantation after multiple thoracenteses for symtomatic relief of persistent right-sided hepatic hydrothorax.
• Patient presented with respiratory distress and left-sided infiltrates consistent with pneumonia on POD #5 after OLT. Patient was started on antibiotics and underwent a right-sided therapeutic thoracentesis with removal of 1.3 liters of fluid.
• Post-thoracentesis chest imaging revealed a large hydropneumothorax that was treated with a small-bore chest tube.
• Diagnostic bronchoscopy was not performed due to the absence of endobronchial obstruction on CT.
• Patient was stable without dyspnea and hypoxemia, so video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery was deferred after consultation with thoracic surgery.
• Patient was discharged home on POD #20 without supplemental oxygen.
• Follow-up chest x-ray 1 month later showed improvement in the hydropneumothorax and a chest x-ray obtained 6 months later showed near-complete re-expansion of the right lung without surgical intervention.

Discharge Instructions:
• Follow-up with liver transplant team as needed.
• Follow-up with primary care physician for ongoing care.

Answer in the form CODE: <letter><digit><digit>

text:
The episode described is a post-transplant admission, but the orthotopic liver transplant itself seems to have happened during this admission, since the discharge is on POD #20. The underlying condition is likely cirrhosis with hepatic hydrothorax. The principal diagnosis would normally be the condition chiefly responsible for the admission, which is the end-stage liver disease that led to the transplant. The cause of the cirrhosis is not given, and the diagnosis section is withheld.

The alternative is that the focus is the complication, the hydropneumothorax after thoracentesis. That is, however, a complication arising after admission, so it would not be the principal diagnosis. The admission was for the transplant.

Hepatic hydrothorax in cirrhosis would be coded K76.7 (hepatorenal) or K74.6 (other and unspecified cirrhosis) with J91* (pleural effusion in conditions classified elsewhere). The underlying cirrhosis code is the likely principal diagnosis, and K74 is the most plausible three-character category.

The question asks for a category and the cause is unknown, so K74 (fibrosis and cirrhosis of liver) is the best fit.

CODE: K74
